chapter: The rhythm section, family and records
title: Second marriage to Lorraine; becoming father and grandfather the same day
summary: He discusses marrying Lorraine, their daughter Barbara, being a father and grandfather at once at the Embers, and his eight grandchildren.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Your wife died here in 19- it was in New York, wasn't it?
That's right, November, and I was right there. ... left you with the children.
I do remember that you married again, a lovely lady, Miss Lorraine. I don't know when that was either. You remember what year you married Lorraine?
I've forgotten. We're trying to find out now; we've been together so long.
That's the way with my wife and I. We roommated so long -
I'm in the process of taking her to Europe with me. We have never had a honeymoon.
Isn't it beautiful - in the 20 years or so.
I'm going to take her to Europe with me and let her go somewhere else and I'll just gad around.
And I want to say I know out of that marriage you have another beautiful daughter, Barbara, the most beautiful child -
JONES 66

Oh, Milt, you forgot something. Milt, you know I was sitting in the Embers nightclub and I was sitting with my wife and my daughter and both of them was pregnant and do you know, I became a father and a grandfather at the same time!
Beautiful! That's your daughter Joanne and your wife Lorraine.
My daughter Joanne had a boy -
The same time as your wife Lorraine had a girl.
And she had a girl, at the same time.
What year was that?

Please, I don't know. They'll be 20 years old May 8th and the funny part about it, Earl Wilson wrote in the column that I bought $400 worth of cigars and I only bought $2 worth of cigars, because I came from the hospital and brought Dick Donahue a cigar and went down to give the chef something downstairs and then got the hatcheck girl something - I only had $2 left. With these two births which was - and everybody knows that I was sitting with my wife, my new wife, and my daughter, two pregnant women. They offered them champagne; they drank Seven-Up and gingerale because at that time across the street the man sent a bottle of champagne. They didn't drink champagne; they drank Seven-Up.
JONES
Now you fortunately here in 1973, you have how many grandchildren now?
I have 8 grandchildren and I'm a great-grandfather.
That's beautiful. On that note I think we can close this session out and just listen to some of this beautiful playing that you did and talk about that, what do you say?
Good.
